overview: The paper unifies Discrete, Gaussian, and Simplicial diffusion through the Wright-Fisher population genetics model, proposing novel parameterizations (Hollow, Sufficient Statistic) and stable sampling techniques to enable cross-domain diffusion training and conditional generation.

modules.name: Wright-Fisher Unification Core
modules.description: Implements the theoretical mapping between the three diffusion types and the Wright-Fisher model. Defines the eigenspace computations for the generator matrix, the embedding derivation for the Gaussian limit, and the time dilation functions for different population sizes.

modules.name: Forward Process Simulation
modules.description: Manages the noising logic for all three domains. Handles the simulation of the Markov process for discrete diffusion, Brownian motion in embedding space for Gaussian diffusion, and the intermediate representation with multinomial sampling for the general Wright-Fisher diffusion.

modules.name: Stable Simplicial Sampling
modules.description: Implements the exact simulation of the Wright-Fisher marginals using the Jenkins-Spanò algorithm for the ancestral process and Dirichlet sampling. Includes the Griffiths approximation for the low-time regime to ensure numerical stability when the standard infinite series fails.

modules.name: ELBO & Loss Computation
modules.description: Calculates the Evidence Lower Bound for each diffusion type. Implements the Poisson KL divergence for discrete diffusion, the squared embedding error for Gaussian diffusion, and the score-matching objective with the specific metric tensor for simplicial diffusion, including the low-t bound.

modules.name: Prediction Parameterizations
modules.description: Implements the specific prediction heads for the neural network. Includes the Hollow Parameterization to resolve ELBO singularities and the Sufficient Statistic Parameterization (SSP) which computes the evidence vectors phi to make the model invariant to time and diffusion domain.

modules.name: Model Architectures
modules.description: Constructs the neural network backbones used for denoising. Includes the Transformer for language models, the CNN for DNA sequence modeling, and the U-Net architecture for image data, ensuring they interface with the unified parameterization logic.

modules.name: Reverse Process & Sampling
modules.description: Implements the generative sampling logic. Handles the reversal of the SDE for simplicial diffusion and the Markov chain for discrete diffusion. Manages the time discretization and the iterative denoising steps from the prior distribution back to the data distribution.

modules.name: Conditional Generation & Guidance
modules.description: Implements classifier guidance mechanisms for conditional sampling. Calculates gradients of log-likelihood for external predictors (e.g., accessibility models for DNA) and integrates them into the reverse process using one-shot or step-wise approximation strategies.

modules.name: Data Processing & Loading
modules.description: Handles dataset-specific preprocessing for DNA, Protein, Language, and Image data. Converts raw data into one-hot vectors, simplex representations, or embedding tensors, and implements custom samplers and data loaders for efficient batching.

modules.name: Unified Training Pipeline
modules.description: Orchestrates the training loop for both individual domain models and the Unified model. Manages the alternating optimization steps for the SSP model where the loss function switches between discrete, Gaussian, and simplicial objectives within a single epoch.

modules.name: Numerical Stability & Precision
modules.description: Manages high-precision arithmetic operations required for the infinite series in simplicial diffusion. Monitors condition numbers for catastrophic cancellation, dynamically switching between standard floating-point operations and high-precision libraries (e.g., mpmath) based on error thresholds.

modules.name: Evaluation & Metrics
modules.description: Computes all experimental metrics including Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) for DNA accessibility profiles, Predicted Local Distance Difference Test (pLDDT) for protein foldability, and Perplexity for language generation.
